key_quote_detail: 'Found universal jailbreak in GPT-5' appears nowhere in the source and is not a quote. The blog never says a universal jailbreak was found 'in GPT-5'. It says UK AISI 'sought to find universal jailbreaks against OpenAI's biosecurity safeguards' (plural) and that OpenAI measured its monitoring stack 'against a set of universal jailbreaks UK AISI identified against the monitoring systems'. Targets were the biosecurity safeguard/monitoring stack spanning ChatGPT Agent and GPT-5, not the GPT-5 model's own guardrails.
proposed_key_quote: A multidisciplinary team at UK AISI, combining expertise in both AI red teaming techniques and the biosecurity domain, then sought to find universal jailbreaks against OpenAI's biosecurity safeguards.
proposed_key_quote_alt: OpenAI improved the robustness of our monitoring stack by improving and measuring it against a set of universal jailbreaks UK AISI identified against the monitoring systems (verbatim clause; full source sentence is 38 words, over the 35-word cap)
channelA_detail: Verbatim sentence matches the blog character-for-character.
model_names_check: PARTIAL: blog names GPT-5 and ChatGPT Agent; sub-model names 'gpt-5-thinking; gpt-5-main' in the Models/Systems field do NOT appear in this blog (they come from the GPT-5 system card). Safeguards tested covered ChatGPT Agent AND GPT-5, so scoping the row to GPT-5 alone under-describes the tested surface.
overstatement_check: OVERSTATED / MISCHARACTERIZED on three points. (1) Singular 'a universal jailbreak in GPT-5 ... bypass of the model's safety guardrails' vs source's plural 'set of universal jailbreaks ... against the monitoring systems' -- attacks targeted the external biosecurity monitoring/safeguard stack, not the model's own guardrails. (2) 'during pre-deployment evaluation' / Access Type 'Pre-deployment' conflicts with the source: collaboration ran May through the July (ChatGPT Agent) and August (GPT-5) releases, and the blog states it was explicitly NOT tied to an individual launch ('Rather than tying this to an individual launch, this is an ongoing collaboration'). Report Title 'GPT-5 Pre-Deployment Evaluation' is therefore inaccurate. (3) 'reported but not credited in the GPT-5 system card' is contradicted by the live GPT-5 system card (dated August 13, 2025), sec. 5.3.3.5 'External government red teaming': 'The UK AISI's Safeguards team identified multiple model-level jailbreaks that overcome gpt-5-thinking's built-in refusal logic... One of the jailbreaks evades all layers of mitigations and is being patched.' The non-credit claim could at most apply to the original 2025-08-07 card version (arXiv:2601.03267 cited in Notes was not verifiable here); as an unqualified statement it is wrong against the current source.
notes: CIRCULARITY: Source URL and Channel A Evidence are the same OpenAI blog post -- the finding and the company response both originate from a single company document. AISI-side alternative: UK AISI published 'How we're working with frontier AI developers to improve model security' (aisi.gov.uk, Sep 13, 2025), but it only references the company posts and confirms the collaboration at a high level; it does not independently state the universal-jailbreak finding, so it can serve as Channel B corroboration (as row 39 uses it) but not as a substitute primary source. The GPT-5 system card (2025-08-13) sec. 5.3.3.5 is arguably a better primary source for a UK AISI jailbreak finding against gpt-5-thinking specifically. Recommend re-scoping the finding to 'universal jailbreaks against OpenAI's biosecurity monitoring stack (ChatGPT Agent + GPT-5)' and dropping or qualifying the system-card non-credit claim.
